# Authenticate callers and sign users in

## Intent

Every request to the Parley REST API is made by a known caller or is refused. This package gives the hub its three credential types (the admin token, the API key of a person and the personal access token of automation), decides for every request who is calling and whether the credential still stands, and gives a person the one way to obtain an API key: signing in through an identity provider with `parley login`, which also creates the user and the user's personal organization the first time.

## Goals

- A request to a non-public route under `/api/v1` passes authentication only with a live admin token, API key or PAT presented as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`; the routes behind it learn the credential's type, its id, its user and, for a PAT, its permissions, paths and workspace binding.
- Every authentication failure is one of five fixed answers: `401` with the message `authentication required`, `invalid credentials`, `credential revoked` or `credential expired`, or `403` with `user is blocked`; revocation, expiry and blocking are reported only after the secret matched.
- The hub stores a hash of each secret and never the secret.
- `GET /api/v1/auth/providers` lists the configured identity providers with an authorize URL, without a credential and without exposing a client secret.
- `POST /api/v1/auth/callback` exchanges an OAuth code for the user and a new API key, creates the user and the personal org at the first login, and revokes the user's older API keys at every login.
- `parley login` signs a developer in through the browser, or stores a credential given with `--api-key`, and saves the hub URL, the credential and the user id to the client configuration file with mode 0600.

## Non-goals

- The rate limit per credential and per client address (PLAT-FR-025, which lies inside this package's range of ids): package 02 http_api_conventions. This package only reports the credential id that the limiter counts by.
- The error envelope, the order of checks, the list shape, the body rules, `Cache-Control: no-store` as the default and the rule that `Idempotency-Key` is ignored on `POST /auth/callback`: package 02 http_api_conventions.
- Loading `config.toml` (`[[oauth.providers]]`, `[server].external_url`), opening the store, creating the admin token and storing its hash and the bootstrap `admin_email`, and scrubbing of credentials from logs: package 03 server_lifecycle_and_configuration.
- The routes `/user`, `/users…` and `/orgs…`, user selectors, the admin check, blocking and unblocking as operations, user and org deletion, and `POST /users` (which reuses the personal-org rule built here): package 05 users_and_organizations.
- Creating, listing, changing and revoking PATs, refreshing and revoking API keys, the scope registry and the scope check, and `paths` validation: package 06 api_keys_and_access_tokens. This package stores the PAT record and authenticates it; it has no route that creates one.
- The workspace access rule: package 07 workspace_access_rule. The binding guard for bound PATs: package 08 workspace_bound_tokens.
- The client configuration file as every command reads it, the global flags, the general rules for output, error printing and exit codes, and the request timeout (PLAT-FR-090 to PLAT-FR-095): package 09 cli_foundation. This package writes the file at login and gives `parley login` the exit codes its own entry states.
- Authentication of git requests, where the credential is the HTTP Basic password: package 17 git_smart_http, which calls the credential check built here.
- A password login, and any other route that creates an API key: not part of the product (PLAT-FR-033).

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new. Package 01 hub_skeleton delivers `parleyd` and `parley` with `internal/server/` and `internal/cli/`. Package 02 http_api_conventions delivers the request pipeline with a position for authentication at step 2 of the check order, the error envelope and the list helper. Package 03 server_lifecycle_and_configuration delivers `internal/config/`, the embedded store in `internal/store/` and the admin-token bootstrap.

The source is `docs/prd/03_platform.md`: PLAT-FR-020 to PLAT-FR-033 (without PLAT-FR-025), §3.3.2 (credential types), the parts of §3.3.3 and §3.3.4 that a login creates and authentication reads, PLAT-FR-035 as far as a login needs it, the routes `GET /auth/providers` and `POST /auth/callback` of §3.5, `parley login` of §3.6, §3.3.7 as far as login writes the file, and the OAuth entries of §3.10.

The code of this package lives in `internal/identity/` (records, credentials, authentication, OAuth client, sign-in, the two routes), `internal/cli/login.go` and `internal/cli/config.go` (the command and the file it saves), `internal/hub/identity.go` (wiring on the composition of package 03) and `test/e2e/login_test.go`.

Because packages 05 and 06 come after this one, this package creates the records a login writes and authentication reads: users, orgs, memberships, API keys and PATs, with the fields of §3.3.3. Packages 05 and 06 add the routes over them.

## Requirements

### Credential types and presentation (§3.3.2, PLAT-FR-020)

| Type | Wire format | Identity |
|---|---|---|
| Admin token | `parley_admin_<64 lowercase hex>` | none (no user) |
| API key | `parley_<key_id>_<secret>`; `key_id` 8 and `secret` 32 characters from `[0-9A-Za-z]` | a user |
| PAT | `parley_pat_<token_id>_<secret>`; `token_id` 8 and `secret` 32 characters from `[a-z0-9]` | a user |

The hub stores only a hash of each secret. A secret is shown once, in the response that creates it. REST calls present the credential as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`; the scheme name `Bearer` is matched without regard to case.

Every route under `/api/v1` needs a credential, except `GET /auth/providers` and `POST /auth/callback`. A public route answers whether or not a credential is sent, and a bad credential sent to it is not refused.

When a request passes, the routes and checks behind authentication learn: the credential type (`admin`, `api_key` or `pat`), the credential id (the fixed id `admin` for the admin token, otherwise `key_id` or `token_id`), the user with role and status (none for the admin token) and, for a PAT, its `permissions`, `paths` and `workspace`. Package 02's rate limit counts by the credential id.

### Authentication answers (PLAT-FR-020, PLAT-FR-021, §3.3.4)

Checks run in this order, and the first that fails decides the answer:

| Check | Failure |
|---|---|
| header present, scheme `Bearer`, token non-empty and of a known format | `401 unauthenticated`, message `authentication required` |
| credential id exists and the secret matches | `401 unauthenticated`, message `invalid credentials` |
| not revoked | `401 unauthenticated`, message `credential revoked` |
| not expired | `401 unauthenticated`, message `credential expired` |
| user not blocked | `403 forbidden`, message `user is blocked` |

Revocation and expiry are reported only after the secret matched, so a caller who knows only an id cannot probe a credential's state: a revoked, expired or blocked user's credential presented with a wrong secret gets `invalid credentials`. Secrets are compared in constant time.

Blocking revokes nothing. While a user is blocked, every credential of that user fails with `403`; once the user is `active` again, every credential that is neither revoked nor expired authenticates again. A credential with `expires_at` null never expires.

The admin token has no user. A route that needs a user (the routes under `/user` and the bound-token mint, which later packages register) answers the admin token `403 forbidden`.

### Identity providers (PLAT-FR-030, §3.5, §3.9)

The supported providers are `github` and `google`, each configured by an `[[oauth.providers]]` entry with `name`, `client_id`, `client_secret` and optional `authorize_url`, `token_url` and `userinfo_url` overrides (for example for GitHub Enterprise).

`GET /auth/providers` is public. It answers `200` with a list of `{"name","authorize_url"}`, ordered by `name`, with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`. `authorize_url` carries the client id and the scopes the hub needs: `user:email` for GitHub (`https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=…&scope=user%3Aemail`), `openid email profile` for Google. The caller adds `redirect_uri` and `state`. Client secrets are never exposed. With no provider configured the list is empty.

### The login callback (PLAT-FR-031, §3.5)

`POST /auth/callback` is public. Its body:

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Validation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` | string | yes | | a configured provider |
| `code` | string | yes | | non-empty |
| `redirect_uri` | string | yes | | see below |
| `expires` | int | no | 90 | 0, 30, 60 or 90 (days) |

`redirect_uri` is allowed when it is `http` on `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` (any port and path), or when its scheme, host and port equal those of `[server].external_url`.

The hub validates the body, validates `redirect_uri`, exchanges the code with the provider, reads the user's identity and then, atomically, upserts the user and issues an API key. Calls to the provider time out after 15 seconds. It answers `200`:

```json
{"user":{"id":"uuid","username":"alice","email":"a@x","full_name":"","role":"user","status":"active",
  "provider":"github","provider_id":"123","created_at":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z","updated_at":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
 "api_key":{"key":"parley_<key_id>_<secret>","key_id":"<key_id>","expires_at":"2026-04-01T00:00:00Z"}}
```

| Status | `error_type` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | missing field, bad `expires`, unknown provider, `redirect_uri` not allowed |
| 401 | `unauthenticated` | the provider rejected the code |
| 403 | `forbidden` | the user is blocked |
| 409 | `conflict` | uniqueness conflict |
| 502 | `upstream_error` | the provider failed, timed out, or returned no user id or verified e-mail |

On every failure nothing is changed: no user, org, membership or key is created and no key is revoked.

### The identity the provider gives (PLAT-FR-031)

The identity MUST include a stable provider user id and a verified e-mail. GitHub's primary verified e-mail is used when the profile hides the address. A missing id or e-mail is `502 upstream_error`. The username is the provider's login or display name, or `<provider>-<provider_id>` when the provider gives none.

### Users at login (PLAT-FR-032, PLAT-FR-035, §3.10)

**New user** (no user with this `provider` and `provider_id`): created `active`. If the username is taken, the hub tries `<name>-2` … `<name>-10`. The role is `admin` when the e-mail equals the bootstrap `admin_email` (ignoring case) and no admin user exists yet; otherwise `user`.

The new user gets a personal org in the same transaction: `name` is the username, `owner_id` is the user, and the user is its first member. The slug is derived from the username:

1. lowercase; replace every character outside `[a-z0-9_-]` with `-`; collapse runs of `-`; trim leading and trailing `-` and `_`;
2. if fewer than 2 characters remain, use `u-<first 8 characters of the user id>`;
3. if it starts with a digit, prefix `u-`;
4. if the slug is taken, try `<slug>-1` … `<slug>-10`.

Examples: `Alice.Smith` → `alice-smith`; `42bob` → `u-42bob`. If no free slug is found, or an org already has the user's name, the login fails with `409 conflict` and nothing is created.

**Existing user** (matched by `provider` and `provider_id`): a blocked user is refused with `403` and nothing changes. Otherwise `email` and `username` are refreshed from the provider. If the new username is taken, the old one is kept silently.

**Both:** every live API key of the user is revoked, including one in use on another machine, and a new key is issued with the requested lifetime. PATs are not touched. A uniqueness conflict (for example an e-mail that belongs to another account) is `409 conflict` and changes nothing.

Constraint (PLAT-FR-033): only the OAuth callback creates API keys. There is no password login.

### `parley login` (§3.6, §3.3.7, PLAT-FR-090)

Flags: `--provider <name>` (default `github`), `--expires <days>` (default `90`; 0, 30, 60 or 90), `--api-key <key | ->` (skip the browser and store this credential; `-` reads it from stdin). The hub URL is the first non-empty value of `--endpoint-url`, `PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL` and the file key `endpoint_url`.

**Browser flow.**

1. Resolve the hub URL. Fetch `GET /auth/providers` and pick the provider.
2. Listen on `127.0.0.1` on a free port. Open the provider's authorize URL in the browser with `redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` and a random `state`. If no browser can be opened, print the URL on stderr.
3. Wait up to 120 seconds for the redirect. A `state` mismatch fails the login. The browser tab shows a short success or failure page.
4. Call `POST /auth/callback`. Save `endpoint_url`, `api_key` and `user_id` to the config file.

**Key flow (`--api-key`).** Call `GET /user` with the credential and, on success, save it. No key is created or revoked. A PAT needs `users:read`. The admin token cannot be stored this way, because it has no user: the hub refuses it.

**Output.** The `User` on stdout as one JSON document indented by 2 spaces; `Logged in as <username>` on stderr.

**Exit codes.** 0; 1 when the hub refuses, with the hub's error envelope printed on stderr as received; 2 for every client-side failure (no endpoint, connection failure, timeout, state mismatch, an invalid flag value, an unreadable or unwritable config file), with an envelope on stderr whose `code` is 0 and whose `error_type` is `usage_error` for a bad flag or argument and `client_error` otherwise.

**The config file.** `$PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml` when `PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR` is set and non-empty, otherwise `~/.parley/config.toml`. Keys: `endpoint_url`, `api_key`, `user_id`. `parley login` creates the directory (mode 0700) and the file (mode 0600). The file is replaced atomically and keeps mode 0600. Keys the CLI does not know are preserved. An unparseable file is a client error (exit 2).

### End-to-end flows

- **First login.** A developer runs `parley login --endpoint-url <hub>`. The CLI fetches the providers from `parleyd`, listens on a loopback port and opens the browser. The developer approves at the provider, and the browser is redirected to the CLI with a code and the state. The CLI posts the code to `parleyd`, which exchanges it with the provider, reads the identity, creates the user, the personal org and an API key in one transaction and answers `200`. The CLI saves the config file with mode 0600 and prints the user. A request to a protected route with the saved key passes authentication as that user.
- **Second login.** The same developer logs in again from another machine. `parleyd` finds the user by provider identity, revokes the first key and issues a second. A request with the first key is answered `401` `credential revoked`; the second key authenticates.
- **Operator.** An operator sends a request to a protected route with the admin token that the bootstrap of package 03 wrote. `parleyd` matches it against the stored hash and passes the request as the admin caller, with no user. The same request without the header is answered `401` `authentication required`.

## Design Decisions

1. **Project decisions relied on.** Go; the store is embedded SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite` behind `internal/store`; HTTP is `net/http`; the CLI is `github.com/spf13/cobra`; tests use `testing`, table-driven, with `net/http/httptest`.
2. **This package owns the identity records.** The tables for users, orgs, memberships, API keys and PATs, with the fields of §3.3.3, are created here through the schema migration of `internal/store`. Why: a login writes the first four and authentication reads keys and PATs, and packages 05 and 06 depend on this one. Agreed with packages 05 `users_and_organizations` and 06 `api_keys_and_access_tokens`: they add no table and no column for these records; they read and write the tables created here.
3. **A PAT can be stored without a route.** `internal/identity` has a function that generates a PAT (id, secret, hash) and stores it for a user with given permissions, paths, workspace and expiry. It takes an open store transaction, generates the id again when it already exists, and validates nothing beyond the record's shape. Agreed with package 06 `api_keys_and_access_tokens`: its minting operation is the one way a PAT is created in production; that operation validates, applies the subset rule and then calls this function for the write. No other package calls this function; this package's tests call it directly to seed PATs.
4. **Secret hash.** The hub stores the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the secret part of an API key or PAT. Why: the secrets are 32 random characters, so a fast hash is enough. The comparison uses `crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` over the two hashes. Ids and secrets are generated from `crypto/rand`.
5. **The admin token's hash belongs to package 03.** Authentication verifies an admin-format token through the verification function of `internal/identity/admin.go`, the file package 03 creates for its bootstrap code, and does not reimplement the hash. A hub that is not bootstrapped answers an admin-format token `401` `invalid credentials`.
6. **A credential is recognised by its exact format**: `parley_admin_` plus 64 characters of `[0-9a-f]`; `parley_pat_` plus 8 and 32 characters of `[a-z0-9]` joined by `_`; `parley_` plus 8 and 32 characters of `[0-9A-Za-z]` joined by `_`. The lengths make the three disjoint. Anything else is "not of a known format".
7. **The header.** The scheme and the credential are separated by one or more spaces; white space around the credential is ignored. A credential in a query parameter, a cookie or another header is not read.
8. **Expiry boundary.** A credential is expired when the current time is at or after `expires_at`.
9. **A route declares that it needs a user.** The declaration is checked right after authentication and answers the admin token `403 forbidden` with the message `this route needs a user`. The authenticator reads the declaration as a named mark of package 02's route registration. This is the one error type and message the admin token gets wherever a route needs a user: packages 05 and 06 use the declaration on every `/user…` route and state the same message, and package 08 answers the same error type and message from its handler on `POST /workspaces/:slug/tokens`, where the access check has to run first.
10. **OAuth uses the standard library only.** The code exchange is one form-encoded `POST` to the token URL with `client_id`, `client_secret`, `code`, `redirect_uri` and `grant_type=authorization_code` and the header `Accept: application/json`; the identity is read with `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`. No OAuth module is added.
11. **Provider endpoints.** GitHub: authorize `https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize`, token `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token`, user `https://api.github.com/user`; the e-mail list is read from the user URL with `/emails` appended. Google: authorize `https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth`, token `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`, user `https://openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo`. The PRD says only "the provider's public endpoints".
12. **Google's `authorize_url` also carries `response_type=code`**, which Google requires; GitHub's carries exactly `client_id` and `scope`, as in the PRD's example.
13. **Rejected or failed.** The provider "rejected the code" (`401`) when the token endpoint answers a JSON object with an `error` member, with any status below 500. Every other outcome without an access token — a network error, a timeout, a status of 500 or above, a body that is not a JSON object — and every failure of the identity read is "the provider failed" (`502`).
14. **Identity fields.** GitHub: `id` (as a decimal string) is the provider user id, `login` the username, `name` the full name; the profile's `email` is used when non-empty, otherwise the entry of the e-mail list with `primary` and `verified` true. Google: `sub`, `name` as the username and the full name, `email` only when `email_verified` is true. A username is used as given after trimming white space; an empty one becomes `<provider>-<provider_id>`.
15. **`full_name`** of a new user is the provider's display name, or empty; it is not refreshed at later logins, because the user can change it with `PATCH /user`.
16. **Username collisions for a new user** that exhaust `<name>-2` … `<name>-10` are a `409 conflict`.
17. **"No admin user exists yet"** counts users with role `admin` in any status.
18. **E-mail and username uniqueness** compare the exact stored strings. Only the comparison with `admin_email` ignores case, as the PRD states.
19. **The personal org is not changed at later logins**: a refreshed username does not rename it.
20. **Key lifetime.** `expires_at` is the issue time plus `expires` × 24 hours; `expires` 0 gives `expires_at` null.
21. **Error messages of the callback are fixed texts** and never contain the code, a client secret, an access token or the provider's response body.
22. **`parley login` reads and writes the config file itself**, in `internal/cli/config.go`, and prints its own errors and exit codes with an error type kept in `internal/cli/login.go`. Why: package 09 `cli_foundation`, which generalises both for every command, depends on this package. Agreed with package 09: it takes both over as the single implementation. It extends `internal/cli/config.go` into the one read and save every command uses, replaces the login command's own error type, request code and printing with its shared client, printers and exit-code mapping, and keeps the behaviour specified here; after package 09 no second copy remains.
23. **Only the flag selects the key flow.** `PARLEY_API_KEY` and the file key `api_key` are ignored by `parley login`; `--expires` and `--provider` are ignored in the key flow.
24. **A provider the hub does not list** fails the login with `client_error` and exit 2, naming the providers the hub offers.
25. **The redirect listener** serves `GET /callback` once and closes. A redirect with an `error` parameter or without `code` fails the login like a state mismatch. `state` is 32 hexadecimal characters from `crypto/rand`. `redirect_uri` and `state` are appended to `authorize_url` as query parameters.
26. **Opening the browser** runs `open` on macOS, `xdg-open` on Linux and `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler` on Windows. The opener and the 120-second wait are parameters of the command's constructor, so tests replace them.
27. **`endpoint_url` is saved without trailing slashes.** `user_id` is the `id` of the returned `User`.
28. **An unparseable config file fails `parley login` before any request**, so that a key is not issued and then lost. A file that cannot be written after a successful callback is exit 2 with a message that says the key was issued and not saved.
29. **TOML** is read and written with `github.com/BurntSushi/toml`, decoding into a map so unknown keys survive. Comments in an existing file are not preserved.
30. **Profile: full**, with three execution paths.
31. **The personal-organization rule (PLAT-FR-035) is owned here.** Login needs it, so this package specifies and builds it: one exported function of `internal/identity` that takes an open transaction, the user's fields (username, e-mail, full name, provider, provider id) and the role, and creates the user, the personal org with its derived slug and the membership, or returns a conflict error. The sign-in chooses the username (the `-2` to `-10` suffixes) and the role before it calls the function. Package 05 `users_and_organizations` calls the same function from `POST /users` with role `user` and does not restate the slug rule.

## Dependencies

- Package 02 http_api_conventions (draft): the request pipeline with the authentication position, public routes, the error envelope, the list helper and the per-route `Cache-Control`.
- Package 03 server_lifecycle_and_configuration (draft): `internal/config` with `[[oauth.providers]]` and `[server].external_url`, `internal/store` with transactions and schema migration, the stored admin-token hash with its verification function, and the bootstrap `admin_email`.
- Identity providers GitHub and Google, over HTTPS, at login only. When a provider is unreachable, login fails with `502`; authentication of existing credentials does not depend on it.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Scope / permission**: A string carried by a PAT that grants read or write access to an area.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it).
- **Path-scoped token**: A PAT whose writes are limited to files matching a list of globs.
- **Admin token**: The operator's credential, written at first boot. It has no user.
- **API key**: The credential of a person at a terminal, issued only by a login.
- **PAT**: A personal access token, the credential of automation; the only one that carries scopes, a workspace binding or path limits.
- **Personal org**: The organization created with a new user, named after the username, with the user as owner and first member.
- **Live**: Of an API key or PAT: neither revoked nor expired.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Credential presentation

**Rationale:** Every later route trusts what authentication reports about the caller, so the three credential types and the two public routes are fixed once.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN a request to a non-public route under /api/v1 carries an Authorization header with the scheme Bearer, in any letter case, and a live admin token, API key or PAT, THE parleyd SHALL pass the request to the next check and report the caller to it: the credential type, the credential id, the user with role and status (none for the admin token) and, for a PAT, its permissions, paths and workspace
   → the route's handler runs and reads a caller {type: "admin" | "api_key" | "pat", credential_id: "admin" | key_id | token_id, user: User or none, permissions: string[], paths: string[] or null, workspace: string or null}; permissions, paths and workspace are set only for a PAT
   Check: integration
   - setup: a test hub: the request pipeline of internal/server with the authenticator and routes of internal/identity installed, over a store opened in t.TempDir()
   - setup: the store is bootstrapped with an admin token through the bootstrap code of package 03
   - setup: user alice (role user, status active) holds a live API key and a live PAT with permissions [git:read], paths [docs/**] and no workspace
   - setup: a non-public test route GET /api/v1/test/whoami that answers 200 with the caller it was given
   ```
   in internal/identity/authenticate_test.go, a table over {admin token, API key, PAT} x scheme {Bearer, bearer, BEARER}: r = get('/api/v1/test/whoami', Authorization: scheme + ' ' + credential); assert r.status == 200; admin: assert r.json.type == 'admin' and r.json.credential_id == 'admin' and r.json.user == null; API key: assert type == 'api_key' and credential_id == key_id and user.id == alice.id and user.role == 'user' and user.status == 'active'; PAT: assert type == 'pat' and credential_id == token_id and user.id == alice.id and permissions == ['git:read'] and paths == ['docs/**'] and workspace == null; one more row with two spaces after the scheme and a trailing space after the credential: assert 200
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF a request to a non-public route under /api/v1 has no Authorization header, a scheme other than Bearer, an empty credential, or a credential that matches none of the three wire formats, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request before any later check runs
   → HTTP 401 with error_type unauthenticated and message "authentication required"; the route's handler does not run
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub: the request pipeline of internal/server with the authenticator and routes of internal/identity installed, over a store opened in t.TempDir()
   - setup: a non-public test route GET /api/v1/test/whoami that answers 200 with the caller it was given and counts its calls

### REQ-2: Credential state

**Rationale:** A revoked, expired or blocked credential must stop working at once, and its state must not be readable by someone who holds only its id.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] IF the secret of an API key or PAT matches and the credential's revoked_at is set, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request
   → HTTP 401 with error_type unauthenticated and message "credential revoked"

1. [REQ-2.2] IF the secret of an API key or PAT matches, the credential is not revoked and the current time is at or after its expires_at, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request

   - setup: the authenticator takes its clock as a parameter
   - setup: a non-public test route GET /api/v1/test/whoami that answers 200 with the caller it was given

1. [REQ-2.3] IF the secret of an API key or PAT matches, the credential is neither revoked nor expired and its user's status is blocked, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request

**Rationale:** A login is the one place an API key is born, and each login leaves the person with exactly one live key.

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A developer signs in for the first time and the saved key works

1. **developer** runs parley login --endpoint-url with the hub's URL
2. **parley CLI** fetches GET /api/v1/auth/providers, listens on a loopback port and opens the provider's authorize URL with its redirect_uri and a random state
3. **parleyd** answers the provider list with the authorize URL built from the configured client id
4. **developer** approves the sign-in at the provider, whose redirect brings the browser to the CLI's listener with a code and the state
5. **parley CLI** checks the state and sends POST /api/v1/auth/callback with the provider, the code and the redirect_uri
6. **parleyd** validates the redirect_uri, exchanges the code with the provider and reads the identity
7. **parleyd** creates the user, the personal org, the membership and an API key in one transaction and answers 200 with the user and the key
8. **parley CLI** saves endpoint_url, api_key and user_id to config.toml with mode 0600, prints the user on stdout and exits 0
9. **developer** sends a request to a protected route with the saved key
10. **parleyd** matches the key's hash, finds the key live and its user active, and passes the request as that user

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd through the Run function of internal/hub on a real TCP listener, the request pipeline of internal/server, internal/identity: routes, OAuth client over real HTTP, sign-in transaction, authenticator, internal/store on a real database file, internal/config reading a real config.toml, internal/cli login with its real HTTP client, redirect listener and config file

**Setup:**

- parleyd started in-process through the Run function of internal/hub on 127.0.0.1:0 with a data directory and a config.toml under t.TempDir()
- a fake GitHub: an httptest server with an authorize page that redirects to the given redirect_uri with a fresh code and the given state, a token URL that turns that code into an access token once, and a user URL; config.toml has one [[oauth.providers]] entry github whose authorize_url, token_url and userinfo_url point at it
- the hub is started with one extra non-public test route GET /api/v1/test/whoami that answers the caller
- the login command's browser opener is replaced by a function that sends a GET to the URL and follows redirects, as a browser does
- PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR is a directory under t.TempDir()
- the fake GitHub's user is {id: 123, login: 'Alice.Smith', name: 'Alice Smith', email: 'a@x'}

**End state:**

- parley login exited 0 and printed a User with username Alice.Smith and status active
- config.toml exists with mode 0600 and holds the hub's URL, a key of the form parley_<8>_<32> and the user's id
- the store holds one user, one org with slug alice-smith owned by that user, and one membership
- GET /api/v1/test/whoami with the saved key answers 200 with type api_key and that user's id
- the same request without an Authorization header answers 401 authentication required

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/login_test.go: code = cli.Run(ctx, ['login', '--endpoint-url', hubURL], stdout, stderr); assert code == 0; u = json(stdout); assert u.username == 'Alice.Smith' and u.status == 'active'; cfg = toml(configDir + '/config.toml'); assert mode(configDir + '/config.toml') == 0600; assert cfg.endpoint_url == hubURL and cfg.user_id == u.id and cfg.api_key matches ^parley_[0-9A-Za-z]{8}_[0-9A-Za-z]{32}$; w = get(hubURL + '/api/v1/test/whoami', 'Bearer ' + cfg.api_key); assert w.status == 200 and w.json.type == 'api_key' and w.json.user.id == u.id; assert get(hubURL + '/api/v1/test/whoami').status == 401; assert the store's only org has slug 'alice-smith' and owner_id == u.id
```

### PATH-2: A second login replaces the developer's key

1. **developer** runs parley login on a second machine, with another config directory, and approves at the provider
2. **parley CLI** sends POST /api/v1/auth/callback with the new code
3. **parleyd** finds the user by provider and provider id, refreshes the e-mail and username, revokes the first key and issues a second one
4. **parley CLI** saves the second key on the second machine and prints the same user
5. **developer** sends a request with the first key from the first machine
6. **parleyd** matches the first key's secret, finds it revoked and answers 401 with the message credential revoked

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd through the Run function of internal/hub on a real TCP listener, internal/identity: routes, OAuth client, sign-in transaction, authenticator, internal/store on a real database file, internal/cli login with its real HTTP client and config file

**Setup:**

- parleyd started in-process through the Run function of internal/hub on 127.0.0.1:0 with a data directory and a config.toml under t.TempDir()
- a fake GitHub: an httptest server with an authorize page that redirects to the given redirect_uri with a fresh code and the given state, a token URL that turns that code into an access token once, and a user URL; config.toml has one [[oauth.providers]] entry github whose authorize_url, token_url and userinfo_url point at it
- the hub is started with one extra non-public test route GET /api/v1/test/whoami that answers the caller
- the login command's browser opener is replaced by a function that sends a GET to the URL and follows redirects, as a browser does
- PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR is a directory under t.TempDir()
- a first parley login has completed with config directory A

**End state:**

- both logins printed a User with the same id
- the key in directory A is answered 401 with error_type unauthenticated and message credential revoked
- the key in directory B is answered 200
- the store holds one user, one org and two API keys, one of them revoked

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/login_test.go: k1 = toml(A + '/config.toml').api_key; set PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR = B; code = cli.Run(ctx, ['login', '--endpoint-url', hubURL], stdout, stderr); assert code == 0; k2 = toml(B + '/config.toml').api_key; assert k2 != k1; assert json(stdout).id == toml(A + '/config.toml').user_id; r = get(hubURL + '/api/v1/test/whoami', 'Bearer ' + k1); assert r.status == 401 and r.json.error.message == 'credential revoked'; assert get(hubURL + '/api/v1/test/whoami', 'Bearer ' + k2).status == 200; assert count(users) == 1 and count(orgs) == 1
```

### PATH-3: An operator calls the hub with the admin token

1. **operator** sends a request to a protected route with Authorization: Bearer and the admin token the bootstrap wrote
2. **parleyd** recognises the admin format, verifies the token against the stored hash and passes the request as the admin caller, with no user
3. **operator** sends the same request with one character of the token changed, and once more without the header
4. **parleyd** answers 401 invalid credentials to the changed token and 401 authentication required to the missing header

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd through the Run function of internal/hub, including the admin-token bootstrap of package 03, the request pipeline of internal/server, the authenticator of internal/identity, internal/store on a real database file

**Setup:**

- a data directory and config directory under t.TempDir(); parleyd is run once with --admin-email boss@x.io, the token is read from the admin_token file and the file is deleted
- parleyd is then started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with one extra non-public test route GET /api/v1/test/whoami that answers the caller

**End state:**

- the admin token is answered 200 with type admin, credential_id admin and no user
- the changed token is answered 401 with message invalid credentials
- the request without a header is answered 401 with message authentication required
- the database file does not contain the admin token

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/auth_test.go: r = get(hubURL + '/api/v1/test/whoami', 'Bearer ' + token); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.type == 'admin' and r.json.credential_id == 'admin' and r.json.user == null; bad = token with its last character replaced by another hexadecimal digit; r = get(…, 'Bearer ' + bad); assert r.status == 401 and r.json.error.message == 'invalid credentials'; r = get(…); assert r.status == 401 and r.json.error.message == 'authentication required'; assert not contains(bytes of the files in the data directory, token)
```

# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `golangci-lint run ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/identity/... ./internal/cli/... ./test/e2e/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `02` — uses the request pipeline's authentication position, public routes, the error envelope and the list helper
- `03` — uses the loaded configuration ([[oauth.providers]], external_url), the store with transactions and migration, and the stored admin-token hash and admin_email

## Tasks

### 1. Authenticate the admin token, API keys and PATs on every non-public route (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1.1, REQ-1.2, REQ-1.3, REQ-1.5, REQ-1.6

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the task's behaviours to internal/identity/authenticate_test.go and internal/identity/credential_test.go, with a test hub helper in internal/identity/testhub_test.go that builds the request pipeline of internal/server over a store in t.TempDir() and registers the test routes whoami and me, and confirm they fail; packages 05 and 06 extend this helper and do not write a second one
- 1.2 Create the identity tables through the schema migration of internal/store: users (id, username unique, email unique, full_name, role, status, provider and provider_id unique as a pair, created_at, updated_at), orgs (id, name unique, slug unique, url, owner_id nullable, status, created_at, updated_at), memberships (org_id and user_id unique as a pair, created_at), API keys (key_id, user_id, secret hash, expires_days, expires_at nullable, revoked_at nullable, created_at) and PATs (token_id, user_id, secret hash, name, permissions, paths nullable, workspace nullable, expires_at nullable, revoked_at nullable, created_at)
- 1.3 Generate credentials from crypto/rand in the three wire formats: an API key as parley_<8>_<32> over [0-9A-Za-z], a PAT as parley_pat_<8>_<32> over [a-z0-9]; store the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the secret part and never the secret; return the full value once to the caller
- 1.4 Add the store functions later packages and the tests use: create a user, issue an API key for a user with a lifetime in days, store a PAT for a user with name, permissions, paths, workspace and expiry inside a transaction it is given, generating the id again when it exists (the store-level write that package 06's minting operation wraps; no other production code calls it), and look a key or PAT up by its id
- 1.5 Recognise a credential by exact format (admin: parley_admin_ plus 64 characters of [0-9a-f]); read it from the Authorization header with the scheme Bearer matched without regard to case, one or more spaces between scheme and credential, surrounding white space ignored
- 1.6 Answer 401 unauthenticated with the message "authentication required" for a missing header, another scheme, an empty credential or an unknown format, and 401 with "invalid credentials" for an unknown id or a secret that does not match; compare hashes with crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare, and run the comparison against a fixed dummy hash when the id is unknown so both cases take the same path
- 1.7 Verify an admin-format token through the verification function of internal/identity/admin.go that package 03 created; answer "invalid credentials" when it does not match or the hub is not bootstrapped
- 1.8 Report the caller to the pipeline: type (admin, api_key, pat), credential id (admin, key_id or token_id), the user with role and status or none, and a PAT's permissions, paths and workspace; expose the same credential check as a function that takes the credential string, so the git server of package 17 can call it with a Basic password
- 1.9 Add the route declaration "needs a user" as a named mark of package 02's route registration, read by the authenticator right after it accepted the credential, which answers the admin token 403 forbidden with the message "this route needs a user"
- 1.10 Install the authenticator in the authentication position of package 02's pipeline and register this package's schema step on the composition of package 03, in internal/hub/identity.go, so every non-public route under /api/v1 is authenticated

**Touches:**

- `internal/identity/schema.go`

### 2. Refuse revoked and expired credentials and the credentials of blocked users (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2

- 2.2 Give the authenticator its clock as a parameter, the system clock in production
- 2.3 After the secret matched, and only then, check in this order: revoked_at set is 401 "credential revoked"; the current time at or after expires_at is 401 "credential expired" (null never expires); a user whose status is blocked is 403 forbidden "user is blocked"

- 2.5 Read the credential and its user's status from the store on every request, so that a revocation, a block and an unblock take effect on the next request and blocking changes no credential record

### 4. Exchange an OAuth code and read the user's identity from the provider (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4

**Depends on:** 3

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the task's behaviours to internal/identity/oauth_test.go, against a fake provider built on httptest that records its requests, and confirm they fail
- 4.2 Add the provider client with one operation that takes a provider name, a code and a redirect_uri and returns an identity {provider, provider_id, username, full_name, email} or an error of the kind rejected or upstream; the HTTP client and the timeout (15 seconds by default) are parameters
- 4.3 Exchange the code with one form-encoded POST to the token URL carrying client_id, client_secret, code, redirect_uri and grant_type=authorization_code and the header Accept: application/json
- 4.4 Treat a JSON answer with an error member and a status below 500 as rejected, and every other answer without an access token (network error, status of 500 or above, a body that is not a JSON object, no access_token) as upstream
- 4.5 Read the GitHub identity from the user URL with Authorization: Bearer: id as a decimal string, login, name, email; when email is null or empty read the user URL with /emails appended and take the entry with primary and verified both true
- 4.6 Read the Google identity from the user URL: sub, name as username and full name, email only when email_verified is true
- 4.7 Trim the username; when it is empty use <provider>-<provider_id>
- 4.8 Return upstream when the user URL or the e-mail list does not answer 200 with the expected JSON, or when the id or the verified e-mail is missing
- 4.9 Bound each call by the timeout and close the connection when it passes; build error texts from fixed words only, never from the code, the client secret, the access token or the provider's body

**Touches:**

- `internal/identity/oauth.go`
- `internal/identity/oauth_test.go`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
- `go test ./... -count=1` passes

### 5. Create the user, the personal org and an API key at a first login (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-5

**Depends on:** 1, 4

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the task's behaviours to internal/identity/login_test.go and internal/identity/slug_test.go and confirm they fail; the handler takes the provider client as an interface so the tests can set the identity it returns, and its clock as a parameter
- 5.2 Register the public route POST /auth/callback, not a create route (so Idempotency-Key is ignored): decode the body {provider, code, redirect_uri, expires}, read the identity through the provider client, and run the sign-in
- 5.3 Sign-in, in one store transaction: look the user up by provider and provider_id; when none exists create the user with status active, the username and e-mail of the identity and the provider's display name as full_name
- 5.4 When the username is another user's, try <name>-2 to <name>-10 in order; when none is free fail with a conflict
- 5.5 Set the role to admin when the e-mail equals the stored bootstrap admin_email ignoring letter case and no user with role admin exists in any status; otherwise user
- 5.6 Derive the personal org's slug from the final username: lowercase, replace characters outside [a-z0-9_-] with -, collapse runs of -, trim leading and trailing - and _; fewer than 2 characters left gives u-<first 8 characters of the user id>; a leading digit gets the prefix u-; a taken slug tries <slug>-1 to <slug>-10 in order
- 5.7 Create the org with name equal to the username, owner_id the user and status active, and the membership of the user, in the same transaction; export this creation as one function that takes an open transaction, the user's fields and the role and returns a conflict error when the username, the e-mail or the provider identity is taken, an org has the username as its name, or no slug is free; the sign-in picks the username suffix and the role before calling it, and package 05 calls it from POST /users with role user
- 5.8 Issue an API key for the user with the requested lifetime (expires_at is the login time plus expires x 24 hours, null for 0, 90 days when absent) and answer 200 {user, api_key: {key, key_id, expires_at}} with timestamps written through internal/server/timefmt of package 02
- 5.9 Answer 409 conflict and roll the whole transaction back when the e-mail belongs to another user, an org already has the username as its name, or no free username or slug is found

### 8. Store a credential with parley login --api-key and save the client configuration file (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-8, REQ-9

**Depends on:** 1

**Steps:**

- 8.1 Add the task's behaviours to internal/cli/login_test.go and internal/cli/config_test.go, against a stub hub built on httptest, and confirm they fail
- 8.2 Use github.com/BurntSushi/toml, which package 03 added to go.mod; add no second TOML module
- 8.3 Create internal/cli/config.go, the file package 09 later extends into the one read and save of every command, and locate the config file: $PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml when the variable is set and non-empty, otherwise .parley/config.toml under the user's home directory
- 8.4 Read the file into a map; a missing file is an empty map; a file that is not valid TOML fails parley login before any request with exit status 2 and a client_error envelope
- 8.5 Save: set endpoint_url (without trailing slashes), api_key and user_id in the map, keep every other key, create the directory with mode 0700 when missing, write a temporary file with mode 0600 in the same directory and rename it over config.toml; on failure remove the temporary file and report client_error with a message that says the credential was accepted and not saved
- 8.6 Add the command parley login to the root command with the flags --provider (default github), --expires (default 90) and --api-key; resolve the hub URL from --endpoint-url, PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL and the file key endpoint_url, in that order; with none, fail with exit status 2 and a client_error that names all three
- 8.7 Key flow, chosen by the flag --api-key alone: take the credential from the flag, or from stdin when the value is -, trimmed; an empty credential is a usage_error; send GET <hub>/api/v1/user with Authorization: Bearer and a 30-second timeout
- 8.8 On 200 save the file, print the User on stdout as one JSON document indented by 2 spaces with a trailing newline, and print "Logged in as <username>" on stderr; exit 0
- 8.9 On a hub error print the envelope on stderr exactly as received and exit 1; on a connection failure or an answer that is not a JSON object print an envelope with code 0 and error_type client_error and exit 2; in both cases print nothing on stdout and save nothing
- 8.10 Give the login command the error type it needs for this (exit status plus envelope) in internal/cli/login.go; package 09 replaces it with its shared error types and exit-code mapping and moves login onto its client

### 9. Sign in through the browser with parley login (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-10

**Depends on:** 7, 8

**Steps:**

- 9.1 Add the task's behaviours to internal/cli/login_test.go, with a browser opener and a wait the test supplies, and confirm they fail; add the first-login and second-login flows to test/e2e/login_test.go with a fake GitHub
- 9.2 Validate --expires (0, 30, 60 or 90) before any request; another value is a usage_error with exit status 2
- 9.3 Fetch GET <hub>/api/v1/auth/providers without a credential and pick the item whose name equals --provider; a hub error is printed as received with exit status 1; an unreachable hub, an unreadable answer or a provider that is not listed is a client_error with exit status 2, the last naming the providers the hub lists
- 9.4 Listen on 127.0.0.1 port 0; build the URL to open by adding redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback and a state of 32 hexadecimal characters from crypto/rand to the provider's authorize_url as query parameters, keeping the parameters it has
- 9.5 Open the URL with the opener (open on macOS, xdg-open on Linux, rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler on Windows; a parameter of the command's constructor); when it fails print the URL on stderr and keep waiting
- 9.6 Serve GET /callback once: a code together with the state that was sent answers 200 with a short HTML success page; another state, an error parameter or a missing code answers 400 with a short HTML failure page and fails the login with client_error, exit status 2; compare the state in constant time
- 9.7 Wait at most 120 seconds (a parameter of the constructor) for the redirect; on expiry fail with client_error, exit status 2; close the listener on every way out
- 9.8 Send POST <hub>/api/v1/auth/callback with {provider, code, redirect_uri, expires} and no Authorization header; a hub error is printed as received with exit status 1
- 9.9 On 200 save endpoint_url, api_key.key and user.id through the config file code, print the user object alone on stdout, indented by 2 spaces, and "Logged in as <username>" on stderr; never print the key
